title: setDesiredAPY commit is mempool-visible: any staker can front-run the commit to lock in a higher (or lower) accPhUSDPerShare than the protocol intends
rootCause: The two-step gate is described as a safety mechanism, but economically it FAILS to deter front-runners: when the owner submits the commit transaction, the new `desiredAPYBps` is fully predictable (it equals the public `pendingAPYBps`), so any staker can frontrun the commit. Because `setDesiredAPY` (commit branch) calls `_updatePool()` THEN `_updatePhUSDEmissionRate()`, the order is: accrue under OLD rate -> set new rate. A front-runner who stakes immediately before the commit lands gets debt-anchored at the OLD `accPhUSDPerShare`; immediately after the commit, the new (higher) rate begins compounding to their advantage. Conversely, a front-runner who claims/withdraws BEFORE a downward commit locks in the higher pre-cut rate.
economicImpact: The two-step gate is economically useless against the very actors it should slow down (sophisticated stakers monitoring the mempool). It only slows down the OWNER and (incidentally) gives MEV bots a 100-block visibility window. Honest passive stakers do not benefit; active mempool-watching stakers and bots capture the difference.
affectedParties: Honest passive stakers (relative loss vs front-runners); protocol intent (the gate was designed to telegraph intent, not to subsidise front-runners).
attackScenario: Owner calls `setDesiredAPY(NEW_HIGHER)` (preview). Public event `IntendedSetAPY(NEW_HIGHER, blockNumber, owner)`.

Up-direction case: MEV bot sees the preview event. Bot stakes a large `phUSD` amount immediately. `_updatePool` runs first, settling the OLD `accPhUSDPerShare`; bot's `phUSDDebt = amount * acc_OLD / PRECISION` is anchored at the pre-commit checkpoint.
Owner's commit lands at block N+1..N+100. `_updatePhUSDEmissionRate` jumps `phUSDPerSecond` upward.
Bot accrues at the NEW rate immediately. Over the next blocks, bot's pending phUSD grows ~`amount * new_phUSDPerSecond * Δt / totalStaked`.
After enough accrual, bot calls `claim()` or `withdraw(all)`. Net: bot captures a disproportionate slice of NEW-rate emissions for capital it deposited only after the rate was known.
Down-direction symmetric attack: bot sees a preview that would LOWER APY, calls `claim()` immediately to lock in OLD rate emissions before the commit lands.
profitability: Profit per upward-APY event ~= bot_capital * (new_rate - old_rate) * holding_blocks * (bot_share / total_share). With a doubling APY change and a few blocks of holding, this is easily a meaningful capture against passive stakers. Cost = gas + capital cost of the short hold.
preconditions: Owner uses a public mempool for the commit transaction.
Public `pendingAPYBps` / `getPendingAPYInfo()` view returns the next value (it does - profile §4.4).
Bot has phUSD or can borrow.

intentMismatchEvidence.documentation: Profile §8.10: 'setDesiredAPY commit is publicly mempool-visible ... Standard MEV; document but not a finding.' But the existence of a TWO-STEP gate implies a security goal beyond standard MEV -- otherwise why bother with the preview? The protocol clearly intends the gate to give stakers TIME to react. Economically, it gives MEV bots time to react, not slow stakers.
intentMismatchEvidence.implementation: The commit branch updates state IN the transaction visible to the mempool; there is no rate-change cooldown for new stakes, no per-user time-weighted accrual, no anti-snipe mechanism.
intentMismatchEvidence.discrepancy: The two-step gate is designed for caution but in practice it (a) doesn't bound the new rate, (b) doesn't slow MEV, (c) doesn't notify users via any on-chain throttle on their next claim/stake. Its only effect is to require a second admin tx -- a UX delay, not an economic safeguard.

mitigations: Use a private mempool (Flashbots Protect, MEV-Share) for the commit tx.

Replace block-based 100-block window with a longer time-based window AND add a rate-change cooldown: stakes within N blocks of a commit accrue at the average of old/new rate or are excluded from the bonus.
Use time-weighted accrual (e.g. weight by stake-block-age) so newly-staked capital cannot snipe rate changes.
Combine with on-chain timelock + public scheduler so the rate transition timestamp is known well in advance and rewards accrue smoothly.
crossReferences: CODE-010 (twoStep-APY-pending-state-not-cleared) - distinct angle: CODE-010 is the state-cleanup spec gap, ECON-004 is the economic MEV failure of the two-step model.
